# impots.tax — Complete French Tax Data Reference

> Site: https://impots.tax
> Last updated: March 2026
> Data year: 2025-2026
> Every number is sourced from official institutions. Unverified data is marked [TODO: verify].
> This file contains all tax data displayed on the site.
> Note: French fiscal terms are kept in their original form where no standard English equivalent exists.

---

## 1. Income Tax (Impôt sur le revenu / IR) — 2026 Schedule (2025 income)

Source: French Finance Law 2026, Service-Public.fr, economie.gouv.fr
Indexation: +0.9% (inflation)

| Bracket (per tax share) | Rate |
|---|---|
| Up to €11,600 | 0% |
| €11,601 — €29,579 | 11% |
| €29,580 — €84,577 | 30% |
| €84,578 — €181,917 | 41% |
| Above €181,917 | 45% |

New in 2026: CDHR (Contribution Différentielle sur les Hauts Revenus), a minimum effective tax rate of 20% for the wealthiest households.

Family quotient: 1 share per adult, 0.5 per child (1 share from the 3rd child).
Cap on family quotient benefit: €1,807 per half-share (2026).

---

## 2. Corporate Tax (Impôt sur les sociétés / IS) — 2025/2026

Source: economie.gouv.fr, entreprendre.service-public.fr

| Rate | Condition |
|---|---|
| 25% | Standard rate, all companies |
| 15% | SMEs, on first €42,500 of profit |

SME reduced rate conditions:
- Revenue ≤ €10M (excl. VAT)
- Fully paid-up share capital
- ≥ 75% held by individuals

Social contribution on corporate tax: 3.3% for companies with revenue > €7.63M and tax > €763,000.

Exceptional surcharge 2025-2026 (large companies): 20.6% between €1B and €3B revenue, 41.2% above. Source: Finance Law 2025, extended to 2026.

Note: Finance Law 2026 raised the reduced rate threshold from €42,500 to €100,000, effective January 1, 2026.

---

## 3. Flat Tax / PFU (Prélèvement Forfaitaire Unique)

Source: Ramify.fr, Shine.fr, Service-Public.fr, LFSS 2026

### 2025 Income (filed in 2026)
| Component | Rate |
|---|---|
| Flat income tax | 12.8% |
| Social levies | 17.2% |
| **Total PFU** | **30%** |

### 2026 Income (filed in 2027) — CHANGE
| Component | Rate |
|---|---|
| Flat income tax | 12.8% |
| Social levies | 18.6% (CSG increase from 9.2% to 10.6%) |
| **Total PFU** | **31.4%** |

Applies to: dividends, interest, capital gains on securities, crypto gains (exemption threshold: €305/year in disposals).

Progressive scale option: available annually (box 2OP). Beneficial if marginal rate ≤ 11%. For dividends, 40% allowance applies only under progressive scale.

---

## 4. VAT (TVA)

Source: impots.gouv.fr, economie.gouv.fr

| Rate | Application |
|---|---|
| 20% | Standard rate (most goods and services) |
| 10% | Intermediate rate (restaurants, transport, renovation) |
| 5.5% | Reduced rate (food, books, energy) |
| 2.1% | Super-reduced rate (press, reimbursable medicines) |

France invented VAT in 1954 (Maurice Lauré). Original rate: 16.85%.

---

## 5. Social Contributions (Private sector employees) — 2025

Source: URSSAF rate schedule 2025, CAPEB 2025

Monthly Social Security ceiling (PMSS): €3,925 | Annual: €47,100 | Minimum wage (gross): €1,801.80

| Contribution | Employer | Employee | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Health, maternity, disability, death | 7.00% | — | 7.00% |
| Pension capped (≤ 1 PMSS) | 8.55% | 6.90% | 15.45% |
| Pension uncapped | 2.02% | 0.40% | 2.42% |
| Family allowances (≤ 3.5 × min. wage) | 3.45% | — | 3.45% |
| Unemployment (from May 2025) | 4.00% | — | 4.00% |
| CSG (on 98.25% of gross) | — | 9.20% | 9.20% |
| CRDS (on 98.25% of gross) | — | 0.50% | 0.50% |
| AGIRC-ARRCO Tier 1 | 4.72% | 3.15% | 7.87% |
| Work accident (average) | ~2.00% | — | ~2.00% |
| FNAL (< 50 employees) | 0.10% | — | 0.10% |
| Autonomy contribution | 0.30% | — | 0.30% |
| **Estimated total** | **~32%** | **~20%** | **~52%** |

### The Journey of €100 (median salary ~€2,400 net, 30% marginal rate)

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| Total employer cost ("super-gross") | ~€230 |
| Employer contributions | −€54 |
| Gross salary | ~€176 |
| Employee contributions | −€26 |
| Net salary before income tax | ~€150 |
| Income tax (withholding) | −€20 |
| Net salary after tax | ~€130 |
| VAT on spending (20% average) | −€22 |
| **Real purchasing power** | **~€108** |

Total extraction rate: ~52% (€100 employer base → €48 purchasing power).

## 6. Fuel Tax

Source: UFIP Énergies & Mobilités, Fipeco (February 2026 data)

### SP95 gasoline price breakdown (~€1.71/liter)
| Component | Amount | % of price |
|---|---|---|
| Crude oil + refining | ~€0.48 | ~28% |
| Distribution + margin | ~€0.21 | ~12% |
| Excise tax (ex-TICPE) | ~€0.67 | ~39% |
| VAT on product | ~€0.15 | ~9% |
| VAT on excise tax | ~€0.13 | ~8% |
| **Total taxes** | **~€0.95** | **~55%** |

Key point: VAT is applied ON TOP of the excise tax. It's a tax on a tax.

Carbon component: frozen at €44.60/tonne CO₂ since 2018 (Yellow Vests movement). Was supposed to reach €100/t by 2030.

---

## 7. Behavioral Taxes

### Tobacco — 2025/2026
Source: French Customs, Revue des Tabacs

Breakdown of a €13 pack:
| Component | Amount | % |
|---|---|---|
| Excise (proportional + specific) | ~€8.50 | ~65% |
| VAT (16.67% inclusive) | ~€2.17 | ~17% |
| Retailer commission | ~€1.34 | ~10% |
| Manufacturer margin | ~€0.99 | ~8% |
| **Total taxes** | **~€10.67** | **~82%** |

Evolution: pack price went from ~€1.50 (1990) to ~€13 (2025), a +766% increase in 35 years.

### Alcohol — 2025/2026
Source: French Customs (BOD N°7614)

| Category | Excise 2026 |
|---|---|
| Spirits (> 18° vol.) | €1,932.42/hlap |
| Beer > 2.8° vol. | €8.24/hl |
| Still wine | €4.19/hl |

Wine is very lightly taxed in France (~€0.03/bottle vs ~€349/hl in the UK). The French wine lobby is historically very powerful.

### Sugar Tax — 2025/2026
Source: LFSS 2025

| Added sugar per hectoliter | Tax per hectoliter |
|---|---|
| < 5 kg | €4 |
| 5 to 8 kg | €21 |
| > 8 kg | €35 |

---

## 8. French Welfare System

### RSA (Revenu de Solidarité Active / Minimum Income) — 2025
Source: Service-Public.fr

| Household | Monthly amount (April 2025) |
|---|---|
| Single person | €646.52 |
| Couple, no children | €969.78 |
| Couple + 2 children | €1,357.69 |

~2 million recipient households. Non-take-up rate: ~30%.

### AAH (Disability Allowance)
Maximum: €1,033.32/month (April 2025). Condition: disability ≥ 80%.

### Unemployment Insurance (ARE)
~57% of daily reference wage. Minimum: ~€31.59/day (~€948/month).

### AME (State Medical Aid for undocumented immigrants)
~466,000 beneficiaries. 2024 budget: €1.386B. Cost per capita: ~€17.91/year. Share of total health spending: ~0.5%.

---

## 9. International Comparison — Tax Pressure

Source: OECD Revenue Statistics 2024

| Country | Tax-to-GDP ratio |
|---|---|
| **France** | **46.1%** |
| Denmark | 43.4% |
| Belgium | 42.9% |
| Austria | 42.7% |
| Italy | 42.1% |
| Sweden | 41.3% |
| Germany | 37.6% |
| United Kingdom | 35.3% |
| OECD Average | 33.5% |
| Canada | 33.2% |
| Japan | 33.2% |
| United States | 27.7% |
| Switzerland | 27.6% |
| Mexico | 17.7% |

France: #1 in the OECD, +12.6 points above average.

### Macro indicators
- Public debt: ~€3,300B (~112% of GDP)
- Public spending: 56.5% of GDP
- Budget deficit 2025: ~5.8% of GDP
- Net minimum wage 2025: €1,426/month

Source: DGFiP, IFRAP

| Indicator | Value |
|---|---|
| Total revenue | €55.3B (2024) |
| Average per taxpayer | €1,082 |
| Cumulative increase over 10 years | +30% |

Rates by city (2025): Paris 20.5%, Lyon 32.44%, Marseille 47.13%, Grenoble 67.92%.

## 11. Furnished Rental / Airbnb (Le Meur Law)

Source: Law n°2024-1039, Finance Laws 2025/2026

| Rental type | Micro-BIC ceiling | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| Unclassified tourist rental (Airbnb) | €15,000 | 30% |
| Classified tourist rental | €77,700 | 50% |
| Long-term furnished rental | €77,700 | 50% |

Major 2025 change: depreciation deducted during the rental period is now reintegrated into capital gains at resale.

---

## 12. Inheritance & Gift Tax

Source: Service-Public.fr, art. 777 CGI

Direct line allowance: €100,000 per parent per child (renewable every 15 years).

| Bracket (after allowance) | Rate |
|---|---|
| Up to €8,072 | 5% |
| €8,072 — €12,109 | 10% |
| €12,109 — €15,932 | 15% |
| €15,932 — €552,324 | 20% |
| €552,324 — €902,838 | 30% |
| €902,838 — €1,805,677 | 40% |
| Above €1,805,677 | 45% |

Non-relatives: flat rate **60%** (after €1,594 allowance).
Life insurance (premiums paid before age 70): €152,500 allowance per beneficiary.

France has the 3rd highest marginal rate globally (after Japan 55% and South Korea 50%), but a low allowance (€100,000) vs USA ($13.6M), Germany (€400,000), or UK (£325,000 + £175,000 residence).

|---|---|

| Net profits (2023) | €4.4B (record) |
| Shareholder dividends | €4.1B |

Concession end dates: 2031-2036. Privatized in 2006 under PM Villepin.

## 15. Capital Gains Outside PEA (S&P 500 from France)

Source: Service-Public.fr, France-USA tax treaty

| Account type | Capital gains tax | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| CTO (brokerage, flat tax) | 30% (2025) / 31.4% (2026) | Unlimited |
| PEA (tax-advantaged, after 5 years) | 17.2% (2025) / 18.6% (2026) | €150,000 |

On €10,000 invested for 10 years (+8%/year): PEA saves ~€1,500 in taxes vs CTO.

US stocks are not directly eligible for the PEA, but European-domiciled synthetic ETFs replicating the S&P 500 are (e.g., Amundi PEA S&P 500).

---

## 16. Tax History Timeline

| Year | Event |
|---|---|
| 1914 | Income tax created. Max rate: 2%. Presented as a "temporary" wartime measure. |
| 1954 | VAT invented by Maurice Lauré. Original rate: 16.85%. |
| 1991 | CSG (social contribution) created. Presented as "temporary." Initial rate: 1.1%, now 9.2%. |
| 1996 | CRDS created to repay social debt. Still active 30 years later. |
| 2018 | Flat Tax (PFU) at 30%. Wealth tax (ISF) replaced by property-only IFI. |
| 2019 | Carbon tax frozen at €44.60/t after the Yellow Vests movement. |
| 2026 | CDHR minimum tax, CSG increase on financial income, Flat Tax → 31.4%. |
